title: The Choir of the Ninefold Court
premise: Sable Galloway, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead through the relics he carves, has spent years hiding his gift while keeping the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things. When the crown's Inquisitors begin hunting the gifted, Sable discovers that a relic he carved years ago contains not one voice but nine—the Ninefold Court, ancient sovereigns whose return would reignite the war that once burned half the world. Hunted by Inquisitor Maren Vale, who carries her own buried gift, Sable gathers an unlikely found family of guild outcasts to decide the Court's fate: release them, destroy them, or become their vessel himself. In the end, Sable chooses neither crown nor Court, shattering the ninefold relic at the cost of his own hearing—and perhaps his life—while his found family carries his legacy forward in a world learning to live without its oldest ghosts.
about_author: Felix Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary artifacts before turning to fiction. They write quiet, bone-deep fantasy about people who hear what history refuses to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Bones
chapters.summary: Sable carves a mourning charm for a grieving widow, listening politely to the dead man's complaints. POV: Sable. Establishes his gift, his craft, and his careful invisibility; emotional beat of lonely competence.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: At the Vellum Guild, Sable records trades: bottled laughter, a door to nowhere, a saint's knucklebone. His mentor Odile hints he asks too few questions. POV: Sable. Beat: comfort within routine, first crack of unease.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Criers announce the Gift-Hunt: all who traffic with the dead must register or burn. The guild goes silent; Odile burns papers. POV: Sable. Beat: fear arriving like weather, the end of safety.

chapters.title: What the Knucklebone Remembers
chapters.summary: Inventorying the vault, Sable touches a relic he carved years ago and hears not one voice but nine, layered like bells—sovereigns of the Ninefold Court. POV: Sable. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile reveals she always knew what Sable was, and that the guild's founder died hiding the same relic. She orders it destroyed; Sable hesitates—the nine are singing to him. POV: Sable. Beat: loyalty versus curiosity.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren Vale arrives in the city, methodical and quietly haunted. She interrogates a bone-singer Sable once knew. POV: Maren. Beat: introduce the hunter as human, sympathetic, dangerous.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sold His Name
chapters.summary: Guild runner Pip, a street kid with a stolen name, warns Sable that informants are watching the shop. POV: Pip. Beat: found-family seed planted; warmth amid tightening noose.

chapters.title: Nine Voices, One Throat
chapters.summary: Alone with the relic, Sable answers the Court. They offer knowledge: the location of every hidden gifted soul in the city—including his friends'. POV: Sable. Beat: temptation dressed as protection.

chapters.title: A Door Kicked In
chapters.summary: Vale raids the guild. Odile covers Sable's escape through the vault's impossible door but is taken. POV: Sable. Beat: guilt, flight, the family scattering.

chapters.title: Underneath the City
chapters.summary: Sable and Pip shelter in the Undercroft, a smugglers' warren run by Brannoc, an ex-soldier who lost a hand and a cause. POV: Sable. Beat: reluctant refuge, grudging alliance.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Odile Vess
chapters.summary: Vale questions Odile, who gives nothing but riddles. Vale begins doubting her own orders when she hears Odile hum a lullaby only Vale's dead mother knew. POV: Maren. Beat: the hunter's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: What Brannoc Buried
chapters.summary: Brannoc confesses he fought in the last suppression of the gifted and burned a village of them; he recognizes the relic's song. POV: Brannoc. Beat: shame shared, trust tentatively built.

chapters.title: The Court Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: The nine sovereigns show Sable visions of the old war—not conquest, they claim, but defense against a crown that feared them. POV: Sable. Beat: history rewritten, moral ground shifting.

chapters.title: Pip's Price
chapters.summary: Pip is caught selling information to feed the group and nearly betrays their hideout before Brannoc intervenes. POV: Pip. Beat: forgiveness tested; family means covering each other's sins.

chapters.title: Vale's Secret
chapters.summary: Vale privately uses her suppressed gift—a touch for truth—to verify a suspect's innocence, then falsifies her report. POV: Maren. Beat: self-betrayal; the hunt corrupting the hunter.

chapters.title: The Relic Thief
chapters.summary: A guild traitor, Corvin, steals the ninefold relic to sell to the Inquisition. The group must recover it or lose everything. POV: Sable. Beat: betrayal from inside the walls.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Bone Market
chapters.summary: A running battle through the night market; Pip takes a knife meant for Sable. They recover the relic; Corvin escapes to Vale. POV: Sable. Beat: blood price of loyalty, stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: While She Sleeps
chapters.summary: Sable sits vigil over wounded Pip, and the dead of the market whisper warnings: the Court lies about the war's beginning. POV: Sable. Beat: doubt deepens; tenderness for the found family.

chapters.title: Odile in Chains
chapters.summary: Odile is sentenced to public burning. Vale requests to conduct the interrogation personally, stalling for time she can't explain. POV: Maren. Beat: conscience versus duty, clock ticking.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The Court offers Sable a bargain: free them, and they will save Odile, heal Pip, restore his hearing fully. All he must do is be their vessel. POV: Sable. Beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Pyre Yard
chapters.summary: The group plans a rescue using Brannoc's soldier knowledge and Pip's knowledge of the city's forgotten ways. POV: Brannoc. Beat: purpose forged from guilt; the family becomes a crew.

chapters.title: Fire and Ash
chapters.summary: The rescue goes wrong. Odile dies buying them seconds, her last words telling Sable the relic must be unmade, not freed. POV: Sable. Beat: grief as catalyst; mentor's final lesson.

chapters.title: Vale Catches Up
chapters.summary: Vale corners Sable alone—and instead of arresting him, asks what the nine really want. Her gift confirms he isn't lying. POV: Maren. Beat: enemy becomes uncertain ally.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Reward
chapters.summary: Corvin delivers false information to the Inquisition's commander, who plans to use the relic as a weapon regardless of consequences. POV: Corvin. Beat: power's corruption embodied; even betrayers become tools.

chapters.title: What the Dead Want
chapters.summary: Sable interrogates the Court through the relic, peeling back their glamour: they were tyrants who started the war to keep their thrones. POV: Sable. Beat: disillusionment; the seduction exposed.

chapters.title: Pip Wakes
chapters.summary: Pip recovers and forces the group to stop deciding things around Sable—he's carrying too much alone. First honest argument, first real unity. POV: Pip. Beat: family as friction that heals.

chapters.title: The Commander's Gambit
chapters.summary: The Inquisition publicly announces it will 'cleanse' the Undercroft. Thousands of hidden gifted will die. Vale realizes her reports armed a massacre. POV: Maren. Beat: horror of complicity.

chapters.title: Defection
chapters.summary: Vale brings Sable the Inquisition's full plans and her own confession. Brannoc wants her hanged; Sable vouches for her. POV: Sable. Beat: mercy as risk; the family absorbs its enemy.

chapters.title: Ninefold Rising
chapters.summary: The relic, handled by Corvin's greed, begins waking on its own; the dead across the city stir, and ordinary people start hearing bells. POV: Sable. Beat: the deadline arrives; no more choices deferred.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: The group descends into the war-vault beneath the city where the Court was first bound, pursued by both Inquisitors and the rising dead. POV: Brannoc. Beat: descent literal and moral; old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Corvin's End
chapters.summary: Corvin, abandoned by the commander he served, tries to barter with the Court itself and is consumed—power eating its servant. POV: Corvin. Beat: cautionary mirror of Sable's temptation.

chapters.title: The Binding Chamber
chapters.summary: They reach the chamber where nine thrones of bone wait. The Court offers everything again: Odile alive, the war undone, Sable whole. POV: Sable. Beat: climax of temptation; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: What Sable Chooses
chapters.summary: Sable refuses. He begins unmaking the relic with his carving tools, giving each sovereign back to true death, voice by voice. The dead of the city fall silent, gratefully. POV: Sable. Beat: sacrifice over salvation.

chapters.title: The Commander's Last Order
chapters.summary: The commander orders the pyres lit anyway. Vale openly defies him, revealing her gift before the assembled Inquisition. POV: Maren. Beat: the hunter becomes the hunted; courage as rupture.

chapters.title: Bells Over the City
chapters.summary: As the ninth voice fades, Sable collapses, his hearing gone. The stirring dead rest. The commander, stripped of his pretext, faces mutiny. POV: Sable. Beat: cost paid; silence as both wound and peace.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: The Inquisition fractures; Vale testifies about the massacre order. Brannoc organizes the Undercroft survivors into something new—not a resistance, a neighborhood. POV: Brannoc. Beat: ashes becoming foundations.

chapters.title: Learning Silence
chapters.summary: Sable grieves the loss of the dead's voices—and discovers, terrifyingly, that he doesn't miss being needed by ghosts. He carves his first charm that holds nothing but memory. POV: Sable. Beat: identity rebuilt without the gift.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: The survivors reopen the Vellum Guild under Pip's chaotic management, trading in merely possible things. Vale, disgraced but free, asks for a place. POV: Pip. Beat: found family formalized; joy after grief.

chapters.title: One Voice Remaining
chapters.summary: On Odile's grave, Sable finds a fresh carving in her style—one last message she left before dying: pride, and permission to live. Whether magic or love left it, he stops asking. POV: Sable. Beat: closure; mystery accepted.

chapters.title: The Choir Dispersed
chapters.summary: A year later, Sable teaches apprentices to carve without listening, and the city remembers the Ninefold Court as a warning, not a longing. He finally signs his work with his own name. POV: Sable. Beat: resolution—identity claimed, power refused, family kept.
